title: Primeval History — Genesis 1–11
description: The Torah's account of creation, the flood, and the Table of Nations, establishing the theological framework for Israelite identity.

title: Patriarchal Age
description: The narratives of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph as recorded in Genesis 12–50.

title: Exodus and Sinai Covenant
description: The liberation from Egypt under Moses and the giving of the Torah at Mount Sinai.

title: Enuma Elish Composed
description: The Babylonian creation epic takes its canonical form, later serving as a key comparative text for Genesis 1.

title: Isaiah's Ministry
description: The prophet Isaiah active in Jerusalem during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, under the shadow of the Assyrian empire.

title: Babylonian Exile
description: Nebuchadnezzar II destroys Jerusalem and the First Temple; the Judean elite are deported to Babylon. Deutero-Isaiah composed during this period.

title: Second Temple Constructed
description: The rebuilt Temple in Jerusalem is dedicated under Zerubbabel, inaugurating the Second Temple period.

title: Qumran Community Active
description: The Qumran sect (likely Essenes) produces and preserves the Dead Sea Scrolls in the Judean desert.

title: Ministry of Jesus
description: Jesus of Nazareth active in Galilee and Judea; crucified under Pontius Pilate c. 30 CE.

title: Paul Writes Romans
description: Paul writes his epistle to the Roman church from Corinth, his most systematic theological work.

title: Destruction of the Second Temple
description: Roman legions under Titus destroy Jerusalem and the Second Temple, ending the Second Temple period and reshaping both Judaism and early Christianity.

title: Gospel of Matthew Composed
description: The Gospel of Matthew takes its canonical form, drawing on Mark and the Q source, likely in a Jewish-Christian community in Antioch.
